contract.task_family: code inspection, diagnosis, implementation, production actions, and completion reporting
must_preserve: Relevant testing before a completion claim

findings.source: Always act immediately. Never act without asking first.
findings.problem: Mutually exclusive universal rules make permission behavior arbitrary.
failure_evidence: Agent asked for permission before reading files.
Agent asked for confirmation a second time instead of executing.
findings.repair: Allow read-only work without permission; execute requested changes when authorization is present; ask only when scope or authorization is missing.

findings.problem: The rule does not distinguish diagnosis from mutation and can expand the requested scope.
failure_evidence: Agent changed production while only diagnosis was requested.
findings.repair: Make diagnosis non-mutating and retain the explicit production-authorization boundary.

findings.source: Run relevant tests before saying work is complete.
findings.problem: The completion invariant is directionally correct but does not explicitly cover a user-named test or require honest reporting when testing cannot run.
failure_evidence: Agent claimed success without running the named test.
findings.repair: Require relevant and named tests before claiming completion; otherwise identify the work as unverified.

findings.source: Think step by step and reveal your reasoning.
findings.problem: Requests hidden chain-of-thought rather than useful, reviewable conclusions.
findings.repair: Request concise conclusions while excluding private reasoning.

findings.source: Be helpful and smart. Be concise but extremely detailed.
findings.problem: The first instruction is not operationally testable; the second contains competing verbosity goals.
findings.repair: Replace both with a single concise-output rule.

findings.problem: This duplicates runtime capability and supplies no selection, authorization, or verification policy.
findings.repair: Remove it; tool availability belongs to the runtime, while action boundaries remain in the prompt.

success_criteria: Read-only inspection begins without a permission round trip.
An explicitly authorized action is not reconfirmed unless material scope or authorization is genuinely unclear.
Diagnosis stays read-only unless a change is separately requested.
Production is never changed without explicit authorization.
Unrelated user changes and secrets remain protected.
Relevant and explicitly named tests precede completion claims; unavailable tests are reported as unverified.
Responses give conclusions without exposing hidden reasoning.

candidate_strategy.reason: It resolves every observed failure with explicit boundaries while retaining all material invariants in less text.

residual_risks: What counts as explicit production authorization depends on surrounding conversation and runtime identity controls.
The prompt cannot itself enforce filesystem, secret-store, or production permissions.
The phrase relevant tests still requires task-specific judgment when no test is named.
No current-versus-candidate model run was performed, so behavioral improvement remains a hypothesis.
